text: Hey everybody, Anthony Alfredo here. I'm
going to take you for a lap around Dover
Motor Speedway. One of my favorite
racetracks of all time, the Monster
Mile, big fast onem concrete racetrack.
And I'll show you there's a couple
different approaches you can have to
this place. One is carrying a lot of
speed in and running a little bit of a
diamond like that by letting the car run
up in the middle so you can carry good
entry speed, get the car to wash up, and
as you tip into the throttle, get it to
rotate back down the hill and straighten
up your exit. But you can also run a
tight line wrapping the bottom of the
racetrack because that helps a lot when
it rubbers up since there's a little bit
more grip down there. See, we'll hit
this diamond one more time. Make sure we
get those apexes. The wall's going to
sneak up on you on exit. So, you really
want to be pointed and you really want
to make sure the car is settled when it
lands because it's a big compression as
you drop 30 ft down in the banking. It's
three stories. So, it's a lot of
compression, a lot of suspension travel.
But now, we're going to try to hold a
tighter line around the bottom. You can
come up a little bit, but when you run
it tighter, you'll see you could really
throttle up through the middle of the
corner and and build your momentum, but
you're going to have to give up a little
bit on exit so that you don't wash out
too much and end up getting into the
wall. So, that's something that's really
important, but that line works really
well, especially for managing your tires
if you're patient enough when you do it.
Uh, and ultimately getting to people's
left rear in the middle of the corner,
packing air on them. And we'll just
check out a green flag pit stop here
just in case you have one because uh
this is probably the hardest track to do
them at. You lift under this bridge
right here. You're going to check up,
use the banking of the racetrack to slow
down, then transition down to the flat.
Make sure you get way left to miss those
pit barrels. But hopefully some of those
tips and tricks help you. Thanks a
Logitech G for the support. And I will
say this track feels amazing with the
debug debox technology haptic system on
my Simpse driving simulator because just
the amount of load on the car and and
the amount of travel you get is pretty
intense compared to other tracks and you
could really appreciate it. So it's not
only more immersive, but it just helps
me get acclimated. And that's why I
think this is one of the most realistic
tracks on the sim as far as correlation
from sim to reality. But with that, I'll
see you all in the next one.
